subject: golden retrievers
one_liner: Clinical-grade biometrics for an animal whose only reading is 'great.'
brand_voice_notes: A serious sports-science wearable company that has raised a Series B to measure a golden retriever's happiness, and has never once got a reading below 100. Copy talks like a performance lab: sample rates, percentiles, recovery protocols. Every number is precise and every conclusion is that the dog is fine. Nobody at the company finds this strange. No dog puns in headlines, no 'pawsome', no winking.

hero.h1: Know exactly how good a boy he is.
hero.sub: Tailmetry is a collar sensor that tracks tail RPM, Joy Load and stick throughput around the clock, then tells you, to four decimal places, that your golden retriever is fine.

features.title: Joy Load, measured continuously
features.blurb: Our proprietary score runs from 0 to 100. Across 41,000 hours of beta data it has read 100 every single time. The sensor works. We had it checked twice.

features.title: Tail RPM telemetry
features.blurb: Optical tail tracking at 240 samples per second. Peak recorded so far: 318 RPM, the moment a stranger in the park said "well, who's this."

features.title: Recovery coaching
features.blurb: Every morning Tailmetry builds a recovery plan from overnight data. Every morning the plan is a nap in a patch of sun. We call it personalized because, technically, it is.

demo_screen_concept: The Tailmetry daily dashboard for a golden named Murphy, dark-mode sports-lab style. A big triple ring shows Joy Load 100, Strain 'chased a leaf' and Recovery 'already recovered'. Below it, an hourly Tail RPM bar chart you can tap for exact readings, and a live event timeline (mail arrived, saw squirrel, ate part of a sock). Tabs switch between Today, Tail, Sleep and Coach. A dog switcher swaps between Murphy, Biscuit and Sergeant Pepper, all of whom read 100. A 'Log event' modal appends to the timeline and recomputes Joy Load from 100 to 100, and a 'Recalibrate sensor' button spins for three seconds and also returns 100.

images.rationale: Dark sports-wearable advertising wants a product-on-athlete hero, so 1 hero (dog wearing the collar). Demo is a data dashboard, so no dedicated demo assets; it reuses the headshots as dog avatars in the switcher. Remaining 3 slots on testimonial headshots of each customer's golden.

design_direction.style: Dark Mode (OLED) sports-science wearable lab, midnight-kennel mode. A performance-tracking app in the Whoop/Oura school: near-black ground, data-dense panels, monospace numerals, concentric activity rings and live waveforms, everything glowing faintly like a device at 3am. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: warehouse aisle signs, shelf tags, pallet beams, member cards, scorecard grids, stitch seams, pencil notes, pennants, stud tiles, brass hairlines, velvet ropes, gum leaf corners, sleep rings with mist shading, zzz chips, 3px ink outlines, hard offset shadows, tennis seams, masonry pins, iridescent gradients, lip buttons, lesson paths. Also absent: daylight backgrounds, paper textures, serifs, condensed signage type, handwriting. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The triple ring: three concentric arcs (gold Joy Load, pink Heart, blue Strain) drawn in SVG, always closed at 100 except Strain, which barely moves. (2) The tail waveform: a live animated sine trace of tail RPM running under the hero and as section dividers. (3) The readout chip: every number sits in a dark pill with a Martian Mono figure, a unit, and a delta that always says +0.0 (ceiling). (4) The collar band: a horizontal rounded strap shape with a small sensor pod, used for the hero device and the highlighted tier.
design_direction.archetype: Real-time / operations landing: hero with live device preview, a key-metrics band, how-it-works features, testimonials, pricing, CTA to the sandbox demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Rings draw in once on load (stroke-dashoffset, 900ms ease-out). The tail waveform scrolls continuously and slowly. Readout numbers tick up from 0 to 100 once. Hover lifts panels by 2px with a faint gold glow. All of it stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Split hero: left column holds an eyebrow readout ('LIVE · MURPHY · JOY LOAD 100.0000'), the H1 in Sora 600 at ~64px, the sub, the gold CTA and a ghost 'open the demo' link. Right column holds the hero photo of a golden retriever wearing the collar in a dark studio, with the triple ring and two readout chips floating over its lower corner. The tail waveform runs full-width under both columns.
